reproducibility.not_byte_for_byte_reproducible: An independent no-cache rebuild does NOT yield a stable image digest. Demonstration in this very correction: the verifier Dockerfile was unchanged and its base is digest-pinned, yet the no-cache rebuild produced sha256:35b47fbb… versus the prior sha256:ae7a327a…. Each RUN layer is stamped with a build-time creation timestamp, so two independent builds always differ in layer history even with identical content. The initial Phase 0 record's 'digests identical across builds' observation held only because that second build reused cached layers (same timestamps); a cache-backed rebuild is not independent reproducibility and is not used as proof here.
reproducibility.debian_not_snapshot_pinned: apt-get update resolves the current Debian trixie package set at build time; ca-certificates/curl/procps versions are not pinned to an apt snapshot.
reproducibility.future_rebuild_rule: Any future rebuild that yields a different image digest must be rescanned (real scanner + canary, both fail-closed) and re-recorded before use; the agent binary checksum gate must still pass.
reproducibility.final_no_cache_build_from_pre_build_comm: both images rebuilt with --no-cache from corrected pre-build commit 39fab1b; agent sha256:34b394a9…, verifier sha256:35b47fbb…

canary_scan.scanner_contract: fails closed: a failed scan, canary build, canary scan, or cleanup is reported as a distinct command failure with redacted diagnostics and a non-zero exit, never CLEAN. Runs as root (--user 0:0) for complete filesystem inspection while preserving the image's configured non-root runtime user. Internal find/grep traversals are monitored (find exit > 0 or grep exit > 1 is failure). Output protocol requires complete FILES, CONTENT, IDENTITY, FIND_EXIT, GREP_EXIT sections. Synthetic token fully redacted.
canary_scan.agent_image: clean (no forbidden files, content, secret env, or installer identity state; identity_state_present=false; find_exit=0, grep_exit=1 [valid no-match]; no internal traversal failures)
canary_scan.verifier_image: clean (no forbidden files, content, secret env; find_exit=0, grep_exit=1 [valid no-match]; no internal traversal failures)
canary_scan.synthetic_secret_canary: clean (secret supplied as build-arg and context file did not leak into the image; full token redacted from diagnostics)
canary_scan.identity_state_absent: the retained agent image contains no /home/agent/.claude directory and no /home/agent/.claude.json; the installer-generated machineID/userID and config backups are removed after the build-time version checks. The scanner's IDENTITY probe reports absent for both images.
canary_scan.scanner_tests: 28 deterministic daemon-free tests covering root inspection, unmasked traversal status, exact protocol validation, environment inspection failures and shape, secret-value omission, temporary-directory cleanup, and full token redaction
canary_scan.supersedes: the incomplete scanner from phase-0-review-corrections that ran as the image-configured non-root user and did not detect internal traversal failures
canary_scan.independent_review_reproduced: the independent acceptance review reproduced the incompleteness: configured user agent, find exit 1 (unreadable paths), grep exit 2 (unreadable paths), yet recorded scan_command_failed=false and CLEAN
canary_scan.limitation: A filesystem scan proves the searched-for forbidden material and named secret bytes are absent; it cannot exhaustively disprove unknown secret bytes without reading every byte of the image.

storage_enforcement.basis: local Docker overlay2 on an ext4 data root with no XFS/project-quota support; Harbor passes storage_mb through only on quota-capable providers. Recorded as a limitation, not a blocker.

limitations: No XFS/project-quota data root; Harbor-managed writable-layer storage is unsupported (declared value retained as task metadata only).
No host firewall certifies the launcher bootstrap declaration; not a Phase 0 blocker.
Independent upstream route attestation is unavailable; effective model/provider remain runtime evidence, recorded when the endpoint exposes them and otherwise unavailable.
The image scan cannot exhaustively disprove unknown secret bytes without reading every byte.
Debian package resolution is not snapshot-pinned; apt-get update resolves the current trixie package set at build time.

Image digests are not byte-for-byte reproducible across independent no-cache rebuilds (layer creation timestamps differ); reproducibility here means pinned content inputs plus a recorded, verifiable retained image identity, not identical digests across rebuilds.

scan_image.py makes in-container traversal fail closed: find and grep write to separate temporary files, their statuses are captured directly with no evidence-producing pipeline, and bounded failure diagnostics are retained
scan_image.py requires an ordered exactly-once protocol: missing, duplicate, out-of-order, or invalid FILES, CONTENT, IDENTITY, FIND_EXIT, or GREP_EXIT sections fail closed
scan_image.py keeps environment inspection fail closed for command failure, malformed JSON, and invalid JSON shape; secret-bearing findings report environment key names without values
scan_image.py fully redacts the synthetic canary token, including its random suffix, and no longer reports a token-derived prefix
